$sources: IS 800:2007 Section 10 (connections: holes, spacing, edges, welds) and Sections 6 and 8 (the connection elements in tension and shear)
source: IS 800:2007 (limit state; the member, bolt and weld strengths are in steelLimitState). This table changes the BNBC 2020 steel table it extends where the connection checks read it: the hole sizes, spacing and edges, the fillet weld sizes, and the resistance factors of the connection elements written as the IS 800 strengths (1/γm and the 1/√3 of shear). The base plate bearing is IS 800 7.4.1 (alpha 9 C9b); the other entries (HSS joints, the column side under flange forces, ponding, bracing) are BNBC 2020's.

sources.phiIS: IS 800:2007 as resistance factors of the shared connection checks: tension yielding 1/γm0 = 0.9091 (6.2), net rupture 0.9/γm1 = 0.72 (6.3.1), plate compression and flexure 1/γm0 (7.1.2, 8.2.1.2), shear yielding Av fy/(√3 γm0) = 0.8748 × 0.6 fy Av (8.4.1), shear rupture 0.9 Avn fu/(√3 γm1) = 0.6928 × 0.6 fu Avn (6.4.1); γm0 1.10, γm1 1.25 (Table 5)
sources.holesIS: IS 800:2007 10.2.1, Table 19: standard clearance holes d + 1 (12-14 mm), d + 2 (16-24 mm), d + 3 (above 24 mm); net areas on the hole diameter d0 (10.2.1)
sources.edgesIS: IS 800:2007 10.2.4.2: least edge and end distance 1.5 d0 (rolled, machine flame cut, sawn or planed edges), 1.7 d0 (sheared or hand flame cut); larger bolts 1.65 d / 1.87 d (SAEngine: 1.5 and 1.7 times d + 3 at 36 mm, rounded up)
sources.maxEdgeIS: IS 800:2007 10.2.4.3: largest edge distance 12 t ε (ε = √(250/fy)); taken as 12 t (ε = 1, E250 steel) with no upper limit in mm
sources.filletIS: IS 800:2007 10.5.2.3, Table 21: least fillet size 3, 5, 6, 8 mm for the thicker part up to 10, 20, 32 mm and above (SAEngine's check passes the thinner part: less strict where the parts differ); 10.5.8.1: the largest size along a square edge t - 1.5 mm
sources.concreteBearingIS: IS 800:2007 7.4.1: the design bearing strength of the concrete under a base plate 0.6 fck (the project's concrete strength read as fck), no φ and no increase for a larger supporting area (SAEngine reading; IS 456 34.4 allows 0.45 fck √(A1/A2) at a column base); alpha 9 C9b
sources.referencesIS: The connection notes name the IS 800:2007 clauses of the strengths and rules the pack replaces; the rules it keeps from the parent are named as BNBC 2020's (steelLimitState connections.parentCode)
